# Intake Brief: Generate Mermaid diagrams for card synergies, staff relationships and upgrade chains (MS-0MUYK5BEC007L61X)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Feature** | **Assignee: Map**
**Producer decisions (2026-10-07, interactive): Q1 = A (docs/tooling artefacts); Q2 = B (named three + community-space extension); Q3 = A (committed `.mmd` + `--check` drift guard).** See Appendix.

## Problem statement

The repo already generates a deterministic Mermaid flowchart of the storyline
graph (`src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` → `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`,
with a JSON manifest and a `--check` drift guard), but no other card dataset is
visualised. Designers, reviewers and new contributors must reconstruct card
synergies, staff coverage, upgrade chains and community-space relationships by
reading 174 CSV rows. Generating the same class of deterministic Mermaid
diagram for these datasets makes each relationship legible at a glance and
keeps the pictures drift-guarded against `src/card-data.csv`.

## Users

- **Content designer / producer** — sees at a glance which cards share a synergy,
  which staff can serve which businesses, and how upgrade chains branch and gate.
  - *"As a designer, I want a Mermaid diagram of card synergies, so I can check
    that every synergy type has a healthy cluster of cards without reading the CSV."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of staff coverage, so I can spot uncovered
    business types or overly broad staff."*
  - *"As a designer, I want a diagram of upgrade chains, so I can see the two-step
    level-1 → level-2 branches and their gates."*
- **Reviewer / balancer** — trusts the committed diagrams because a drift guard
  fails when they fall out of sync with `src/card-data.csv`.
- **New contributor / developer** — uses the diagrams as an entry point to the
  card model, alongside `card-catalog.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Diagram generator CLI.** A new dev-only npm script (e.g. `npm run
   docs:diagrams`) generates Mermaid from `src/card-data.csv` through the typed
   card model under `vite-node`, supporting `--diagram
   <synergies|staff|upgrades|community-spaces|all>` (default `all`), `--format
   mermaid|json` (default `mermaid`), `--out <path>` and `--check` (drift guard:
   exit `1` on drift, `0` when up to date). Verified by unit tests that invoke
   the CLI and assert its exit codes and output.
2. **Committed artefacts & drift guard.** Four deterministic Mermaid artefacts
   are committed under `docs/main-street/` — `card-synergies.mmd`,
   `staff-relationships.mmd`, `upgrade-chains.mmd`,
   `community-space-relationships.mmd` — and a Vitest drift guard regenerates
   each from `src/card-data.csv` and fails when the committed file differs
   byte-for-byte. The existing `storyline-graph.mmd` drift guard continues to pass.
3. **Card synergy diagram content.** Shows every business and community-space
   card and all six synergy types (Food, Culture, Service, Commerce,
   Entertainment, Health), with an edge per card↔synergy membership so cards that
   can chain adjacency bonuses are identifiable. Verified by unit tests asserting
   the exact node set plus edges for representative multi-synergy cards (e.g.
   `biz-cafe` → Food + Culture; `cs-public-art` → Culture + Entertainment) and
   that all six synergy types appear.
4. **Staff relationship diagram content.** Shows every staff card, each synergy
   type and named business it may serve (`allowedBusinessTypes`, resolved through
   the existing `getAllowedBusinessTypesForStaff` / `staffMatchesBusiness`
   helpers), and the specialization-skill catalog from `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts`
   (categories and skills). Verified by unit tests asserting representative staff
   edges (e.g. `staff-health-safety` → Health only; `staff-chef` →
   Cafe/Diner/Delicatessen/Food) and that every catalog skill appears.
5. **Upgrade chain diagram content.** Shows each upgradeable business/community
   space as a chain root plus each applicable upgrade, ordered by
   `requiredLevel`/`maxLevel` and labelled with `newDisplayName`, so level-1
   branches and the level-2 gate are visible. Verified by unit tests asserting the
   four level-2 chains (e.g. Bakery → Patisserie / Bread Factory → Grand
   Bakehouse) and that a level-2 upgrade is only shown after a level-1 step.
6. **Community-space diagram content.** Shows each of the eight community-space
   cards, its synergy types and any community-space upgrade (`targetBusiness`),
   including ongoing cost/buff fields where set. Verified by unit tests asserting
   all eight cards and their types.
7. **Determinism & safety.** Two builds from the same CSV are deeply equal, output
   is sorted and contains no timestamp/RNG/wall-clock input, the generator adds no
   runtime dependency (dev tooling only), and Mermaid remains the source of truth
   (artefacts are never hand-edited). Verified by unit tests.
8. **Documentation.** A new `docs/main-street/card-diagrams.md` documents every
   diagram (what it shows, how to read it) and the regeneration command, and
   `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines.md` and
   `src/README.md` link to it. All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
   entries.
9. **Tests, build and full suite.** `npm run build` succeeds and the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Mermaid is the source of truth.** The committed `.mmd` files are generated
  artefacts; never hand-edited. `src/card-data.csv` is the data source.
- **No new runtime dependency.** The generator is dev tooling only, mirroring
  `storylines:graph`; nothing enters the game bundle.

# Skip empty end-of-turn phases (MS-0MUYT436C005B4QN)

## Problem statement

The end-of-turn presentation (the phased income choreography
`animateIncomePhases`) always iterates all five phases — base, synergy,
reputation, events, upcoming — showing each phase label and consuming a fixed
`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` (2200 ms) gap even when a phase has nothing to
contribute. Empty phases add dead time and meaningless labels to every end of
turn (e.g. an "Events" phase when no event fired). The show should skip a
phase outright when there is nothing happening in it.

## Users

- **Players** finishing a turn who want the end-of-turn show to stay tight —
  no pauses or labels for phases with no activity (e.g. no event, no upcoming
  delta, no synergy).
- **Maintainers** who need a single scheduling rule driven by per-phase
  activity so empty phases never consume show time.

Example user stories:

- "As a player, when my turn has no events and no upcoming-card deltas, I want
  the Events and Upcoming phases skipped so the end-of-turn show ends sooner
  instead of pausing on labels for nothing."
- "As a maintainer, I want the phase schedule to reflect what actually
  happened, so an empty phase never adds `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` to the show."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1: Empty phases are skipped.** In `animateIncomePhases`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts`), any phase (base, synergy,
  reputation, events, upcoming) with no non-zero contribution across the
  producing slots is skipped: no phase label is shown and no inter-phase gap
  is consumed for it. A phase is "empty" per the existing per-case
  predicates: base = no slot with `baseIncome > 0`; synergy = no
  `synergyPhaseFlights`; reputation = no slot with `repBonus > 0`; events =
  no `eventDeltaEffects`; upcoming = no slot with a non-zero `upcomingDeltas`
  entry.
- **AC2: Non-empty phases are unchanged and stay ordered.** Scheduled phases
  run in the canonical order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming)
  with the standard `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` gap between consecutive scheduled
  phases; the `collect` phase always runs after the last scheduled phase
  (immediately when every phase is empty, so the day never hangs). Per-phase
  coin/reputation flight behaviour, the credited-total invariant and the
  reduced-motion / replay / headless exemptions are unchanged.
- **AC3: The show compacts and the doc is updated.** Total show length equals
  the sum over scheduled phases only, superseding the fixed ~11 s pacing note
  in `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` for empty phases (non-empty
  pacing unchanged); the note is updated to reflect skip semantics. The
  competitive per-seat closing inherits the same behaviour via the shared
  `animateIncomePhases` path.
- **AC4: Phase reporting stays consistent.** `onPhase` fires only for
  scheduled phases plus `collect`; the index reported is the scheduled
  position (empty phases are not reported), and no external caller regresses
  (single-player and competitive flows share the one function).
- **AC5: Tests cover the new behaviour.** At least one automated test asserts
  empty phases are skipped (no delayed label/gap) and non-empty phases keep
  order and gaps; existing animator tests that encode the old fixed schedule
  (e.g. synergy-only timing in `income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts`) are
  updated to the skip semantics.
- **AC6: Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`
  (the pacing-invariant note and the phased-show description).
- **AC7: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only.** VFX and scheduling only — never mutates engine state,
  the transcript or the credited totals; failures are swallowed so the turn
  always advances (existing non-blocking contract).
- **Reduced-motion / replay / headless** behaviour is unchanged (their
  exemptions sit inside `runIncomePhase`; skip logic must not reintroduce
  flights there).
- **Phase order and per-phase pacing for scheduled phases** must not change.
- **Empty-phase detection must reuse the existing per-case predicates**
  (avoid a second, divergent definition of "empty").
- Engine end-of-turn phases (`InvestmentResolution` → `IncomePhase` →
  `IncidentPhase` → `EndCheck`) are explicitly **out of scope** — they are
  required for engine correctness and cannot be skipped (see Appendix Q1).

## Existing state

- `animateIncomePhases` (`src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` ~line 330)
  builds the five-entry `phaseMeta` list and schedules every entry with a fixed
  `INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS` (2200 ms) gap, always calling
  `showIncomePhaseLabel` + `runIncomePhase`; each `runIncomePhase` case
  already early-returns when its phase is empty. Total show ≈ 11 s
  (`4 × gap + collection`), pinned in
  `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` as "MUST NOT be shortened".
- `onPhase` is fired for each phase (with its `phaseMeta` index) plus one
  `collect` event (index = `phaseMeta.length`); used by browser tests to
  assert ordering.
- The competitive per-seat closing (`MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`)
  concatenates seats' `perSlotBreakdown` and calls the same
  `animateIncomePhases`, so a change here applies to both flows.

## Desired change

- Compute a per-phase activity predicate from the resolved `slots` (reusing
  the same conditions each `runIncomePhase` case uses), filter `phaseMeta` to
  active phases, and schedule only those contiguously — an empty phase shows
  no label and consumes no gap. Schedule `collect` at the end as today
  (`startAt` preserved). Keep `onPhase`'s contract coherent for scheduled
  phases.
- Update the pacing note in `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` and the
  affected animator/browser tests; add skip coverage.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — core change in
  `animateIncomePhases` (per-phase activity predicate + contiguous scheduling,
  label suppression); `runIncomePhase` and `showIncomePhaseLabel` mostly
  unchanged.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — `IncomePhaseOptions`/`onPhase`
  semantics if the emitted index needs to reflect the scheduled position.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` — verify inheritance
  (likely no change; same `animateIncomePhases` call).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — update phased-income-show
  description and the pacing-invariant note.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-animation.browser.test.ts` — synergy-only
  timing assertion (base 0, expects synergy 600 ms after start) must be
  updated; add empty-phase skip assertions.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-sequential-animator.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/income-collection.browser.test.ts` — verify/update
  schedule and collection assertions under skip semantics.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I` "Perform end of turn phase for each player" — the
  competitive per-seat closing that calls the same `animateIncomePhases`
  (inherits the skip behaviour; its "short and skippable" motivation aligns).
- `CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ` epic — the phased income show this change modifies.
- `CG-0MTR766U6003RZ88` — sequential one-card-at-a-time animator pacing
  (per-phase gap semantics).
- `CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS` — the upcoming phase routing (upcoming-delta
  emptiness predicate).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — phased income presentation doc that
  pins the pacing invariant being superseded.
- Signal: `MS-0MV2DORIC001Y9XZ` / `MS-0MV2DPSVB004B1WX` — prior
  income-collection test failures show these animator/browser tests are
  sensitive to schedule changes; update them deliberately.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Test churn**: existing animator/browser tests encode the old fixed schedule
  (e.g. synergy-only timing, sequential-animator delayed-call counts) and will
  need deliberate updates — a prior income-collection test failure pair
  (MS-0MV2DORIC001Y9XZ / MS-0MV2DPSVB004B1WX) shows these tests are sensitive.
  Mitigation: treat test updates as part of this change, not incidental churn.
- **Divergent "empty" definition**: skipping predicates must reuse the exact
  conditions already inside each `runIncomePhase` case, or the show could skip
  a phase the flights would have populated (or vice versa).
- **`onPhase` index semantics**: external consumers (browser tests) read the
  reported index — changing it to the scheduled position must be verified.
- **Scope creep**: engine phase transitions, competitive text summaries and
  any UX redesign of the phase labels are explicitly out of scope (recorded as
  follow-ups, not implemented here).
- Assumption: the ~11 s fixed total is a nominal figure from 5 phases × 2200 ms;
  the exact post-skip duration is not a target — only that empty phases are
  removed.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUXLGCQC000W7ZE** – Add test cases for AI and human win threshold in competitive mode (completed)
- **MS-0MUNB5D7K001GH19** – Visual storyline authoring editor (open)
- **MS-0MUYFX8V3005VEOG** – Test per-seat closing animation sequencing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: end, events, iterate, nothing, over (+5 more)
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — matched: end, events, nothing, over, phase (+4 more)
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — matched: end, events, nothing, over, phase (+4 more)

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which sequence should skip empty phases — the presentation phased
  income show, the engine closing phases, or also the competitive per-seat
  closing?" — Answer (producer): "A — the presentation phased income show
  (`animateIncomePhases`)." Source: interactive reply 2026-10-14. Note: the
  competitive per-seat closing calls the same function, so it inherits the
  behaviour (no separate engine/competitive change).
- Q2: "Skip semantics — fully skip (no label, no gap, show compacts) or keep
  total duration fixed?" — Answer (producer): "A — fully skip; no phase label
  and no inter-phase gap consumed." Source: interactive reply 2026-10-14.
- Q3: "The doc pins phase pacing as 'MUST NOT be shortened' — does skipping
  empty phases supersede that note?" — Answer (producer): "A — yes; skipping
  shortens the show and the doc note is updated." Source: interactive reply
  2026-10-14.
- Assumed (producer may correct): empty-phase definition per existing
  per-case predicates (AC1); reduced-motion/replay/headless unchanged; engine
  phases out of scope (they are required for correctness).

# Intake Brief: Improved money/reputation animation

**Work item:** MS-0MUYT57J80021CWW · `feature` · `medium`

## Headline

When coins and reputation pips fly to the HUD they currently land on
hard-coded coordinates (`gameW * 0.25 + 70` for coins, `gameW * 0.5` for
reputation at `hudY`) instead of the actual on-screen position of the
"Coins: N" / "Reputation: N" numbers. The flights must end at the location of
the painted coin/reputation number.

## Problem statement

The HUD strip renders `Coins: N` left-aligned at `hudLeft + 10` and
`Reputation: N` left-aligned at `favourBandRight + 40` (positions derived from
the SLL layout and viewport, not fixed fractions of the screen width). Every
market of the codebase that animates coins/reputation to the HUD instead targets
static hard-coded fractions of `gameW`, so the landing point only coincidentally
coincides with the counters — and drifts (most noticeably for reputation, whose
number sits near the right of a label that can be wider than the assumed
position) whenever `hudLeft`/`favourBandRight` or the number of digits change.
The animation reads as coins "missing" the counter.

## Users

- **Player.** When a turn ends and coins/reputation resolve, the flying
  visuals should land on the counter numbers so the income visibly accrues
  into the player's totals.

### Example user story

> As a player, when I end a turn and coins/reputation fly to the HUD, I want
> them to land exactly on the Coins/Reputation numbers so I can see the income
> arrive in my totals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Accurate landing.** Every coin/reputation → HUD flight lands within a
   small tolerance (≤ 2px) of the on-screen centre of the corresponding
   numeric value — the coin number for coin flights, the reputation number for
   reputation pips — across the supported viewports and digit counts. This
   covers: end-of-turn income collection (`animateIncomeCollection` +
   `collectIncomeGrids`), the `upcoming` income phase (HUD coin/rep
   destinations), incident-reveal delta bubbles, and the sell refund coin fly.
2. **Single source of truth.** The HUD render publishes one live anchor for
   the coin number and one for the reputation number; all animators consume
   the published anchors. No `gameW * 0.25` / `gameW * 0.5` target literals
   remain in `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimator*`.
3. **Layout drift resilience.** Anchors are recomputed whenever the HUD is
   re-rendered (including viewport/window changes), so subsequent flights
   target the current number positions.
4. **Presentation-only.** The change never mutates game state, the turn
   transcript, or the deferred-mutation window; reduced-motion and
   replay/headless modes remain flight-free exactly as today. No change to
   flight pacing, staggered SFX, or the income-phase choreography.
5. **Tests + docs.** Unit tests assert flight destinations equal the published
   anchors (coin and reputation paths); a browser test asserts the published
   anchor matches the rendered number centre of `coinText`/`repText`. All
   related documentation is updated (including `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`
   and code comments). Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Presentation-layer only (defensive `try/catch` style preserved — a failing
  animator must never stall the turn).
- Must not change phased income pacing (~11s collection) or the
  `incomeCollectionActive` / deferred-delta timing windows.
- Must not regress the HUD layout geometry guards
  (`hud-strip-layout`, `hud-market-geometry-guard` browser suites).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` lays out `Coins: N` at `hudLeft + 10`
  and `Reputation: N` at `favourBandRight + 40`, computing
  `repX = repText.x + repText.width / 2` (centre of the whole label, not the
  number) and passing `coinX: hudLeft + 70` to `animateHudValueChanges`.
- Animators hard-code HUD destinations as fractions of `gameW`:
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomeCollection` (`coinX =
    gameW * 0.25 + 70`, `repX = gameW * 0.5`), `runIncomePhase` `upcoming`
    (`hudCoin`/`hudRep`), `collectIncomeGrids` (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — sell refund (`coinX = gameW * 0.25 + 70`).
  - `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — delta bubbles (`hudCoinX`/`hudRepX`).

## Desired change

- During HUD render, compute and publish the live coin-number and
  reputation-number anchor positions (numeric glyph centre, i.e. label
  origin + prefix width + number-width/2) — e.g. new fields on `SceneLayout`
  or transient scene fields set by `refreshHudStrip`.
- Replace the hard-coded flight destinations with the published anchors,
  falling back to the current approximate coordinate only when the anchor is
  not yet available (e.g. very first render).

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — compute + publish coin/reputation number anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — extend `SceneLayout` (or add scene fields) for the anchors.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — consume anchors in `animateIncomeCollection`, `runIncomePhase` (`upcoming`), `collectIncomeGrids`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorBoard.ts` — consume coin anchor for the sell refund flight.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — consume anchors for incident delta bubbles.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — anchor storage/reset lifecycle.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-animator.test.ts`, `upcoming-flow-animation.test.ts`, `incident-reveal-animator.test.ts`, `sell-demolition-animator.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/hud-strip-layout.browser.test.ts` — destination assertions.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — document the anchor source of truth.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8** — "Coin and Reputation should count up/down"
  (in-progress, idea): end-of-turn reconciliation coins/rep fly to/from the
  HUD totals and the totals should count up/down as the animation plays.
  Complementary: that item animates the *numbers*; this item fixes where the
  flights *land*. Do not duplicate.
- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** — "Visual representation of reputation" (completed).
- **MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB** / **MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ** — reputation income coin
  sources (pedestrian dissolve); origins only, destinations unchanged here.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** — Upcoming/incident delta-flow routing (the

# Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge cards)

## Problem statement

Business and community-space cards are currently rendered with a neutral dark-grey
face (`#2f2f2f`); only a faint synergy-accent header bar, the 64×64 art backing and
the synergy icons carry the synergy colour. Players therefore cannot read a card's
synergy type — or, for a bridge card, both of its synergy types — directly from the
card face, which weakens at-a-glance planning when the market row mixes single- and
multi-synergy cards. The card face should be coloured by synergy type, and bridge
cards (exactly two synergy types) should show both colours, split top and bottom.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — scanning the market row and their street,
  wants to identify a card's synergy type(s) instantly without reading the icon row or
  opening a tooltip.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player scanning the market, I want each business/community-space
  card coloured by its synergy type, so that I can tell Food from Culture at a glance.
- As a Main Street player evaluating a bridge card, I want to see both of its synergy
  colours (top and bottom), so that I immediately understand it connects two clusters.
- As a player with colour-vision deficiency, I still want an unambiguous cue (the
  synergy icons), so that colour is not the only signal.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Single-synergy face colour.** Every business and community-space card with
  exactly one synergy type renders its card face in that synergy type's face colour
  from a single shared, documented palette, replacing the current neutral `#2f2f2f`
  face. The mapping is the single source of truth used by every generator.
- **AC2 — Two-tone bridge face.** Every card with exactly two synergy types renders
  its face split horizontally into two colour bands — **top band = first entry in
  `synergyTypes`, bottom band = second entry** — using the same palette. The rounded
  card corners and the existing inner gradient / header-bar treatments are preserved,
  and neither band bleeds outside the rounded rectangle.
- **AC3 — Both synergies identifiable; colour is not the only cue.** Each bridge card
  continues to render **both** synergy icons (bottom-left), and the title/stat text
  remains white and legible on both bands; cards remain identifiable under hand
  overlap (~20 px) and street stacking (~23 px) (existing layout contract
  CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN). Cards with zero synergy types (event / upgrade / staff) keep
  their existing family colours unchanged.
- **AC4 — All render paths agree.** The static Node generator
  (`generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`), the runtime CSV fallback
  (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the dynamic state-aware generator
  (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) all produce the same synergy colouring/split, and the
  pre-baked SVGs in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` plus
  `csv-checksum.json` are regenerated.
- **AC5 — Tests.** Unit tests cover: single-synergy cards use the matching palette
  colour; bridge cards emit two bands with the correct top/bottom palette colours and
  band geometry; zero-synergy cards are unchanged; the TS and mjs generators agree;
  and the shipped static SVGs reflect the colouring (regression guard). Existing SVG
  tests (`card-svg-generator.test.ts`, `mjs-svg-generator.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`,
  currency/ongoing-cost tests) continue to pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, `README.md` where relevant, and the Main Street docs
  (`docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` bridge section and any card-rendering/design
  notes).
- **AC7 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Rendering-only:** no engine, rules, scoring, adjacency, balance, or card-data (CSV)
  changes. `synergyTypes` is already the source of truth.
- **One palette:** a single documented synergy→face-colour map is the source of truth.
  The `.mjs` static generator cannot import the TS module, so the values are duplicated
  in the two places with a test asserting agreement — following the existing pattern
  used for staff cost text.
- **Two types maximum today** (CSV distribution: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge,
  135 none). Behaviour for >2 synergy types is out of scope; the implementation must
  degrade safely (e.g. fall back to a single/first colour) rather than throw.
- **Preserve the existing card layout:** 64×64 left-art zone, text positions, cost
  badge, level badge, synergy icons and embedded art (CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN).
- **UK English** in code comments and documentation.

## Existing state

- Runtime cards are rasterised from static SVGs generated by
  `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` (`generateCardSvg`) and refreshed
  from the CSV at runtime by `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`
  (`src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts`), driven by `MainStreetSvgTextureManager`.
- `familyColor()` (mjs) and `cardColorScheme()` (TS) give business and community-space
  cards a neutral face (`#2f2f2f`); synergy colour is applied only to the graphic
  backing (`opacity 0.42`), the 20 px header bar (`opacity 0.18`) and the synergy icons.
- `synergyColor` (bright palette) is used for icons/accents; `CARD_BG` (dark palette)
  exists in the TS generator for `generateBusinessCardSvg` and is currently the only
  place a synergy-coloured face is used.
- 39 business/community-space cards: 29 single-synergy, 10 bridge — Cafe, Food Truck,
  Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga Studio, Physiotherapist,
  Teahouse, Public Art.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg` (dynamic) is used only by tests today; the runtime texture
  path is the CSV/static pair — but it must stay consistent.

## Desired change

- Introduce a documented synergy→face-colour palette (reuse `CARD_BG`) and a helper
  that computes the face background: one colour for single-synergy cards, a top/bottom
  colour pair for bridge cards.
- Update the `.mjs` and TS generators to paint the face with that helper, splitting
  bridge faces horizontally (top = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom = `synergyTypes[1]`)
  inside the rounded rect (clip path or two rounded/clipped rects).
- Regenerate the static SVGs and `csv-checksum.json`.
- Add/update tests and documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — face background via palette +
  top/bottom split for bridge cards; expose the mapping for tests.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `cardColorScheme` /
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and `generateBusinessCardSvg` face colouring + split;
  shared `CARD_BG` palette.
- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — canonical `synergyColor` (bright palette) reference;
  add the dark face palette here if it should be shared.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/*.svg` — regenerated, especially
  `biz-cafe.svg`, `biz-food-truck.svg`, `biz-gallery.svg`, `biz-spa.svg`,
  `biz-florist.svg`, `biz-juice-bar.svg`, `biz-yoga-studio.svg`, `biz-physio.svg`,
  `biz-teahouse.svg`, `cs-public-art.svg`.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated checksum.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetSvgTextureManager.ts` — read-only; verify the runtime CSV
  fallback picks up the colouring (no change expected).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — face-colour + bridge split
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — static-SVG regression guard for the
  split + TS/mjs agreement.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — verify no regression in art embedding with the
  new backgrounds.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — document the colour scheme / bridge two-tone rule.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUDYQQ2E00913QN` (completed) — Synergy tooltip.
- `MS-0MTSAWSME004BH6S` (completed) — Add images for all cards.
- `MS-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K` (completed) — Competitive rendering: owner-coloured street,
  shared-market phase alternation, SFX.
- `MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327` (completed) — Move level label to left (same SVG layout code).
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` (open) — Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card
  (touches the art backing in the same generator).
- `MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF` (open) — Identify different AI players (shared
  colour-blind-friendliness concern).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (palette):** use the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette for the card face
  (readable with white text), keeping the bright `synergyColor` palette for
  icons/accents. The producer may prefer the bright palette — a small, localised switch.
- **Assumption (split):** horizontal split, top band = first entry in the CSV
  `synergyTypes` order, bottom = second, matching the operator's "top and bottom".
- **Assumption (scope):** applies to business + community-space cards in all three
  generators; event/upgrade/staff keep family colours; no >2-synergy cards exist today.
- **Risk (generator drift):** the mjs and TS generators hold separate copies of the
  colour logic. Mitigation: shared constant values plus an agreement test.
- **Risk (contrast/readability):** full colour faces may reduce text contrast,
  especially under the 0.18 header overlay. Mitigation: dark palette, keep the synergy
  icons as a secondary cue, and visually check in the browser test.
- **Risk (stale static assets):** forgetting to regenerate the static SVGs / checksum
  leaves the game showing old faces. Mitigation: regenerate in the same change and add
  a shipped-SVG regression test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** card-art redesign, per-owner tile tints, or synergy-icon
  additions are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive round was run — the operator's seed directive plus repo research
sufficed to draft a clear brief. The design defaults below are recorded as **assumed
(recommended option)**; the producer may override any of them before implementation.

- **Q1 (palette):** "Which palette should colour the card face?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): the existing dark `CARD_BG` palette (Food `#5D4037`,
  Culture `#1565C0`, Commerce `#2E7D32`, Service `#6A1B9A`, Entertainment `#C62828`,
  Health `#00838F`), because white card text stays legible; the bright `synergyColor`
  palette stays for icons/accents. Source: repo research of
  `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.CARD_BG` and `MainStreetCardsUtils.synergyColor`.
  Status: **assumed**.
- **Q2 (split):** "How are a bridge card's two colours arranged?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): horizontal split, top band = `synergyTypes[0]`, bottom band =
  `synergyTypes[1]`, matching the operator's wording "two colours top and bottom".
  Source: operator directive. Status: **assumed**.
- **Q3 (scope / render paths):** "Which cards and which generators?" — Answer (agent
  default, recommended): business + community-space cards in all three generators
  (static `.mjs`, runtime CSV TS, dynamic TS); event/upgrade/staff unchanged. Source:
  repo research. Status: **assumed**.

**Research summary (agent, 2026-10-08):** Verified via CSV that bridge cards are the 10
cards with two `synergyTypes` entries and that no card has more than two; located the
two runtime render paths (`MainStreetSvgTextureManager` → static SVGs +
`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow`) and the test-only dynamic `generateBusinessCardSvg`;
confirmed the current face is neutral `#2f2f2f` with synergy only in the accent/header/
icons.

# Allow multiple possible outcomes from storyline nodes

## Problem statement

A storyline choice node currently declares exactly **two** labelled outcomes
— "Accept" (yes) and "Reject" (no), each pointing at one successor card
(`hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`, `rejectNextCardId` in `src/card-data.csv`).
Authors cannot express richer branches, and a chosen outcome always leads to
the same next card. The goal is to let a node present an **arbitrary number
of labelled outcomes**, where each outcome holds a **set of candidate
successor cards** and the actually-visited successor is selected **uniformly
at random** when the player picks that outcome. Producer direction
(2026-10-14, interactive reply): Q1=B (arbitrary labelled player options,
engine picks the successor from an option's candidate set at random);
Q2=A (extend CSV authoring + author CLI + validator + graph/manifest/schema,
**no backward compatibility** required, mermaid documentation must be
re-worked); Q3=A (uniform selection via the seeded `state.rng()`, one draw
per selection at resolution time so replay/Monte-Carlo stay deterministic).

## Users

- **Content/engine authors** — need to declare multi-outcome nodes with
  random branch targets from CSV without programmatic registration.
- **Players** — see an arbitrary labelled option list instead of a forced
  Accept/Reject; repeat plays of the same storyline can take different
  successor paths.
- **Balance team** — benefit from Monte-Carlo determinism being preserved
  (same seed ⇒ same branch), so the existing harness remains comparable.

Example user stories:

- As a content author, I can declare a node with three outcomes
  ("Negotiate", "Walk away", "Escalate"), each listing two possible next
  cards, so a single choice can fan into varied consequences.
- As a player, when I pick an outcome the game resolves to a uniformly
  random one of that outcome's candidate successors, without me choosing the
  next card.
- As a balance engineer, I can re-run a seeded simulation and observe the
  same random branch taken, so storylines remain auditable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Arbitrary labelled outcomes.** A storyline choice node can declare an
  arbitrary number (≥ 1, including > 2) of labelled options authored via CSV
  (`src/card-data.csv`), each option carrying its own ordered candidate list
  of successor card ids (empty list = the chain ends).
- **Uniform random selection.** When an option is chosen, exactly one
  successor is drawn uniformly at random from that option's candidate set
  using the seeded `state.rng()` (one draw per selection, at resolution
  time); replaying with the same seed produces the same successor, and the
  option list the player sees is unchanged by the draw.
- **Legacy shape removed.** The two-way `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/
  `rejectNextCardId` fields and their compiled Accept/Reject semantics are
  replaced by the arbitrary-outcome model (no backward compatibility kept);
  the five shipped storylines are migrated, with the timeline of the change
  documented in the work item.
- **Tooling consistency.** The authoring CLI, static validator
  (`validate-storylines.ts`), graph/manifest export and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` all model the new
  option/successor-set shape, rejecting dangling targets, empty option lists
  and malformed option encodings.
- **Documentation regeneration.** Mermaid graphs, per-storyline documents
  (`docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`), the storyline reference
  (`docs/main-street/storylines.md`) and any doc-drift tests/SVG artefacts
  are regenerated to show the new multi-outcome nodes and pass their drift
  guards.
- **Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover compilation, resolution (random
  draw semantics incl. a seeded replay pair), validator and CLI authoring;
  the storyline regression harness plus the full project test suite pass
  with the new changes.
- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
  site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Determinism: successor selection may consume RNG only from the seeded
  `state.rng()` stream, exactly one draw per selection; `pushChainCard`
  stays RNG-free. Any additional draw shifts the stream and must be pinned
  by tests, so cross-build Monte-Carlo comparisons after this change are not
  numerically identical to before (acceptable — see Risks).
- No backward compatibility: legacy fields, compiled Accept/Reject shape and
  `'accept'`/`'reject'` transcript/save tokens may be removed; a graceful
  path for old saves must still be decided (load-and-drop vs. require a new
  game) and documented.
- The generalised `StorylineOption` seam (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`)
  remains the single compilation/resolution point; the AI and UI paths flow
  through it unchanged in structure.
- CSV authoring must keep the deterministic, machine-parseable, validator-
  gated style of the existing tooling.

## Existing state

- Choice data lives on `EventCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) and is
  authored in `src/card-data.csv` via `hasChoices`, `acceptNextCardId`
  (Accept/"yes", effect `apply`) and `rejectNextCardId` (Reject/"no",
  effect `skip`); legacy fields compile to a two-option `StorylineOption`
  list in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`.
- A programmatic registry (`registerStorylineOptions`) already supports
  arbitrary labelled options with `condition` / `successorResolver`
  callbacks; content authoring via CSV has never used it.
- Resolution: `resolveIncident` defers the choice into
  `pendingEventChoice`; `resolveEventOption`/`resolveEventChoice` apply the
  effect policy and push the single successor (`pushChainCard`, no RNG).
  `decideEventChoice` picks an option index on the AI path; transcript
  records `'accept'`/`'reject'` tokens (`MainStreetTranscript.ts`); saves
  store the `chosenOption` token (`MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`).
- The shipped graph has five storylines; the manifest, Mermaid flowchart,
  per-storyline SVG docs and the schema are regenerated via
  `npm run storylines:graph…` and covered by drift guards and
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`.

## Desired change

- Extend the CSV data model so a row can author an arbitrary labelled option
  list, each option with an ordered candidate successor set. Suggested
  encoding (exact column layout TBD in planning, kept deterministic):
  a single `options` column of the form `label|cardA,cardB;label2|cardC`
  (option separator `;`, label/ successors separator `|`, candidate
  separator `,`), replacing the three legacy columns; `hasChoices` derives
  from a non-empty list.
- Change the compiled model: `StorylineOption` gains a candidate successor
  list (`successorIds: string[] | null`) in place of the single
  `successorId`; `resolveStorylineOption` draws one uniform candidate via
  `state.rng()` at resolution time, applies the option's `effectPolicy`, and
  pushes the drawn card. `successorResolver` (if present) keeps precedence
  over the random draw, and `condition` keeps draw-time filtering with the
  frozen snapshot.
- Migrate the five shipped storylines to the new model, update the
  validator, author CLI (`storyline-author.ts`), graph/manifest export,
  JSON schema, transcript/save/undo tokens, AI decision handling and UI
  option presentation as needed, and regenerate all graph/SVG/doc artefacts.
- Record follow-ups (not in scope): weighted outcomes, per-candidate
  conditions, UI redesign of the option dialog. See Related work.

## Key Files

- `src/card-data.csv` — replace `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` with the arbitrary `options` column; migrate five storylines.
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` choice fields; `StorylineOption.successorId` → candidate successor list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — compilation of CSV options, uniform draw via `state.rng()`, resolution precedence (resolver > random > none).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution path, transcript token, `resolveEventChoice` indexing.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — validate arbitrary option model (labels, successor sets, dangling targets, empty lists).
- `src/scripts/storyline-author.ts` — author CLI for multi-outcome nodes.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `src/scripts/render-storyline-graph*.ts` — edges per option → each candidate successor; Mermaid/SVG re-render.
- `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` — node options + edge model.
- `src/MainStreetTranscript.ts`, `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — option-label tokens, save/undo.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI option pick over arbitrary lists (static chain eval re-worked).
- `src/MainStreetStorylineUi.ts`, `src/MainStreetStorylineJournal.ts` — option label presentation.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md`, `docs/main-street/storylines/*.md`, graph artefacts in `docs/main-street/assets/` — regenerate; drift guards.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/storyline-*.test.ts`, `storyline-regression-harness.test.ts`, `storylines-doc-drift.test.ts`, `MainStreetEngineEventChoice.test.ts`, `storyline-graph.test.ts`.

## Related work

Move the tutorial step "Costs and Reputation" (T13) so it sits immediately before "Move the Library to hand" (T18), where the Library is actually visible in the market row, and strengthen its text to explain why reputation matters (a higher reputation brings more customers and grows income).

## Problem statement

The tutorial step `T13` ("Costs and Reputation", `tutorial.T13.body`) explains that some cards build reputation instead of earning coins, referencing the Library (`cs-library`). ## Users

New players following the built-in onboarding tutorial.

- As a new player, I want the "builds reputation" explanation to appear at the moment I see the Library in the market, so the text refers to something I can actually see.

Deferred, low-priority follow-up to `MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38` (Create a card shader). The card shader is being delivered now as a Canvas-compatible effect (Option A). A true GPU shader (Phaser 4 Filters / custom shader programs) requires the WebGL renderer.

## Goal

Move the game from `Phaser.CANVAS` to WebGL (`Phaser.AUTO`/`Phaser.WEBGL`, with Canvas fallback) so that Phaser 4's Filter system and custom shaders become available, and re-enable a true GPU card shader.

## Known scope / risks

- `main.ts` and `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` pin `type: Phaser.CANVAS`.
- `GeometryMask` is **Canvas-only in Phaser 4** (`node_modules/phaser/src/display/mask/GeometryMask.js:27`). It is used by Main Street (`MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` log + street-map masks, `MainStreetScene.logContentMask`) and shared core UI (`core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`, `Overlay.ts`, `SettingsPanel.ts`) plus gym scenes — all must migrate to the `Mask` filter / `AddMaskShape`.
- WebGL supports only NORMAL/ADD/MULTIPLY/SCREEN blend modes (of 27); Main Street uses none of the exotic ones.
- WebGL context loss/restoration is a new failure mode; canvas-based SVG textures (`textures.addCanvas` in `core/src/core-engine/SvgHelpers.ts`) and `generateTexture` outputs must survive GPU re-upload.
- CI/test strategy: `createCardGame` documents Canvas as ~10x faster than WebGL under SwiftShader; `TestGamePool` forces Canvas and all browser tests boot Canvas. At least one WebGL browser project (Playwright Chromium + SwiftShader) is needed to exercise WebGL-only features.
- Rendering output is not byte-identical across Canvas/WebGL/GPUs; thumbnail/visual-regression determinism needs re-checking.

## Note

Phaser 4.0.0-rc.7 currently ships only WebGL (no WebGPU). This migration is the necessary intermediate step towards a future WebGL2/WebGPU backend, but it does **not** deliver WebGPU.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — refine at intake/plan)

1. The game boots under WebGL with a working Canvas fallback and no regression to existing rendering.
2. All `GeometryMask` usages are migrated to the Phaser 4 `Mask` filter (or an equivalent), across Main Street and shared core UI.
3. At least one WebGL browser test project runs in CI and exercises a WebGL-only feature.
4. Full project test suite passes.
5. All related documentation is updated.

# Console noise when running the tutorial (tf factory + zone collision warnings)

## Problem statement

Starting (and playing) the Main Street tutorial floods the browser console with developer warnings that are not actionable: `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory for key "income-positive-chime" ...` and repeated `Zone collision for "<hand|endTurnButton|incidentQueue>" while composing "main-street-canonical" with "main-street-tutorial" ...`. The noise obscures genuine errors and breaks "clean console" expectations for the tutorial boot path, while gameplay itself is unaffected.

Seed context: browser client console log captured while running the tutorial (`client:789`, 2026-10-10).

## Users

- **Developer / QA engineer** running the tutorial locally who needs a clean console so real errors are visible.
- **Automated browser tests / release checks** that treat unexpected console errors/warnings as failures.

Example user stories:

- As a developer, I want booting and playing the tutorial to emit no unexpected console warnings, so that any real error stands out immediately.
- As a QA engineer, I want the remaining intentional diagnostics to be explicit and quiet by default, so that I do not re-triage known-benign warnings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Booting/playing the tutorial at the canonical 1280×720 viewport emits **no** `[tfAdapter] Missing tf factory ...` warning for the four intentionally factory-less SFX mappings (`sfx-income-positive`, `sfx-income-negative`, `sfx-income-neutral`, `sfx-challenge-complete`), while each of those keys still falls back to the WAV path (verified by test).
2. Booting the tutorial emits **no** `Zone collision ...` warning for `hand`, `endTurnButton`, or `incidentQueue` when composing `main-street-canonical` with `main-street-tutorial`, while the `sceneWins` result still resolves the tutorial zone rects (verified by test).
3. Unexpected diagnostics remain detectable: a genuinely missing factory or an unapproved zone collision can still be surfaced/asserted by tests rather than being silently swallowed (verified by test).
4. At least one regression test asserts the tutorial boot path produces no warnings from either source; `tests/main-street/tfFallback.test.ts`, `core/tests/ui/screen-layout-compose.test.ts`, and `tests/main-street/tutorial-layout-resolution.test.ts` all still pass.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing WAV/Phaser fallback for factory-less SFX keys (engine contract CG-0MUU9PSWC009CW76) — no silent drops.
- Do **not** add new ToneForge recipes/factories in this item (larger separate effort; see risks).
- Preserve `sceneWins` composition semantics and the tutorial alignment contract documented in `MainStreetTutorialHints.ts`; tutorial zone rects must not change.
- The fix must not blind future diagnostics — intentional cases are suppressed/deduplicated, not the detection removed.

## Existing state

- `core/src/core-engine/tfAdapter.ts` (`createTfPlayer`) defaults to a `console.warn` logger. `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` calls `createTfPlayer(tfModule)` / `createTfPlayer(loadedModule)` without a logger, so every factory-less key warns on play.

- Make the intentional audio fallback silent (or debug-level, one-shot) in production wiring, while keeping the fallback behaviour and the ability to surface unexpected missing factories.

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source)

**Related:** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (Make card packs available in the browser
distribution — introduces the pack-source registry this builds on)
**Related:** `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (Make card-pack assets self-contained)

## Summary

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, once `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` lands, a bundled
build-time registry. This item adds a **remote pack source** so a pack catalogue
can be hosted at a URL and fetched at runtime — enabling packs to be published
or updated without rebuilding or re-releasing the game.

This is the future-work half of the source-registry design: the registry seam
(`PackSource[]`) is introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`, and this item
implements the remote provider on top of it.

## Goal (user story)

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack (and its catalogue) at
> a URL, so I can publish or update packs for an installed game without
> rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want a remote pack to appear in the Card Packs panel and
> behave exactly like a bundled or content-directory pack (lock → purchase →
> enable → deal), while the game still boots and plays offline on its bundled
> packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` that fetches a pack
   manifest from a configured URL (via the loader's existing `fetchManifest` /
   `fetchCsv` transports) and contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Define how remote source URLs are declared — a build-time
   config constant, a launcher-provided setting, or a well-known manifest URL —
   and how multiple remote sources compose with bundled/static ones.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Define ordering and conflict handling when the same
   pack id appears in more than one source (bundled wins? first wins? reject
   duplicates?). The core merge contract already rejects duplicate card ids
   whole; pack-id precedence must be decided explicitly.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Decide whether remote
   packs may be ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable or serving a
   malformed manifest must degrade to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never block boot, never blank the listing. Define a timeout.
6. **Trust and integrity.** Address the supply-chain surface: remote packs
   inject card rows into the pool, and the merge contract validates the header
   and duplicate ids but not malicious content. Define an integrity mechanism
   (signing, checksum pinning, allow-listed host/ids) and what the game does
   when verification fails.
7. **Caching / offline.** Decide whether remote packs are cached (for example in
   `localStorage` / Cache Storage) so a previously fetched pack remains usable
   offline, and how cache invalidation/versioning works.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, degradation, gating and
   integrity with tests, and document the remote-hosting contract.

## Acceptance criteria (to be confirmed at intake)

1. A pack catalogue hosted at a configured URL is discovered at runtime and its
   packs appear in the Card Packs panel.
2. Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across lock → purchase →
   enable → deal, and save/load.
3. With the remote host unreachable/slow, the game boots on bundled packs and
   warns; the listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad header/duplicate id is
   rejected whole with a warning, without affecting other sources.
5. Pack-id precedence across sources is deterministic and documented.
6. The integrity mechanism rejects a tampered/unverified remote pack and
   documents the failure mode.
7. Remote pack art resolves and renders (coordinated with
   `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`).
8. Documentation covers configuration, the hosting contract, integrity and
   degradation.
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline (a natural follow-up).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; without integrity
  checks a hostile pack could inject arbitrary card data. Mitigation: signing /
  checksum pinning / host allow-list, with a safe refusal mode.
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the game.
  Mitigation: bounded timeout, non-blocking discovery, bundled-first.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack may lose
  it offline. Mitigation: explicit caching decision.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than re-architecting.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source registration and merge ordering.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — URL contentDir / transport use.
- `core/src/core-engine/CardPackManifest.ts` — manifest parse (shared).
- `vite.config.ts` / config — remote source URL declaration.
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, degradation, integrity tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.
